title: Adaptive Probe Deprioritization and Quota-Based Load Contracts for SLO-Preserving Failover
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Problem: During regional failover and noisy autoscaler flapping, aggressive liveness/readiness probe failures cause mass instance terminations and cascade capacity loss, jeopardizing token latency SLOs and producing long multi-region recovery tails.

Goal: Implement an adaptive probe-deprioritization layer combined with explicit per-tenant quota-based load contracts so that when health signals indicate region stress we (a) temporarily deprioritize non-critical probes and synthetic checks, (b) admit traffic according to contractual quotas (priority classes), and (c) engage token-weighted circuit breakers to maintain tail latency SLOs while preserving minimal throughput.

Key ideas: 
- Probe Deprioritization: dynamically reduce probe frequency and tighten failure hysteresis for low-impact checks (metrics collection, non-blocking readiness hooks) while keeping critical liveness gates intact.
- Quota-Based Load Contracts: assign per-route/tenant load budgets that are enforced during degraded mode. Budgets expressed as tokens/minute or percent of baseline capacity; higher-tier customers receive reserved quota.
- Token-weighted Circuit Breakers: requests consume budget tokens based on request cost (seq-length, priority tag). When budgets are exhausted, shed lower-priority traffic gracefully with structured error responses and retry guidance.
- Observability & Rollback: surface a degradation surface in the Console with per-tenant contract usage, degraded-rate, and predicted SLO impact; allow manual and automated rollback policies tied to SLO signals.

Trade-offs: Adds complexity to readiness logic and admission path; requires careful migration of probe types classification and upfront enforcement rules to avoid latent regressions. But expected to dramatically reduce autoscaler thrash and reduce time-to-recovery in cross-region failovers.
acceptance_criteria: Probe classifications (critical | advisory | synthetic) mapped for all runtime services and documented in Confluence.
Deprioritization controller prototype deployed to canary region and able to change probe frequency/hysteresis without restart.
Quota enforcement middleware implemented and able to reject or degrade requests with clear structured errors (X-Redwood-Degraded header + JSON reason).
Integrated telemetry: per-tenant quota usage, shed-rate, and tail latency (p95/p99) shown in Console dashboards for the canary cluster.
Chaos test: simulated regional CPU pressure + probe jitter shows <=10% increase in p99 vs baseline while preventing >30% scale-in churn across nodes.
Runbook updated with degradations, rollback criteria, and manual override steps.
updates: 2026-02-25 - Ticket created by Aisha Khatri. Initial design sketch attached; motivation from last cross-region incident postmortem.

2026-02-28 - Architecture sync: decided to implement deprioritization as a separate control-plane controller that emits per-service probe policies to agents. Agreed to avoid modifying core kube-probes to keep rolling upgrades safe. (Notes: design doc link below).

2026-03-03 - Spike completed: prototype controller toggles probe frequency and hysteresis via runtime flags; observed 18% reduction in probe-triggered restarts under synthetic noise. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289
2026-03-07 - Product review: PM asked for explicit per-tenant default quotas and migration story; added quota schema and Console UX stub. UX will show ’contract burn’ with projected SLO impact.
2026-03-10 - Integration work started: quota middleware wired into routing layer for canary region; token cost model implemented for text-generation (cost = base + tokens_out * weight).

2026-03-14 - Canary deploy to eu-west-1-internal: observing contract enforcement logs; early dashboards show shedding on low-tier keys without impacting enterprise reserved quotas. Next: run controlled chaos (cpu spike + network spike) and evaluate autoscaler churn.
telemetry_queries: metric:probe-triggered-restarts -> rate() by region and service
trace:degraded-response-path -> p95 latency + sampled traces tagged degraded=true
test_plan: Unit tests for quota token accounting and token cost function edge cases (zero-length, extreme seq-length).
E2E in k8s canary: run controlled high-probe-noise generator and assert scale-in events <= threshold.

Chaos experiment: introduce region CPU saturation and flaky network; assert p99 latency SLOs degrade gracefully less than defined threshold and autoscaler doesn't thrash more than baseline multiplier.
Backward compatibility: validate that older agents ignore new deprioritization controller without crashing.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy controller in passive mode (observe-only) to two canary clusters for 2 weeks. Phase 2: enable active deprioritization for advisory probes + quota enforcement in canary region only; monitor for 48h. Phase 3: widen to additional regions with automated rollback if p99 increases >15% or scale-in churn increases >2x. Add per-tenant opt-out during ramp. Manual override toggle exposed in Console.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mis-classifying a critical probe could delay detection of real failures. Mitigation: conservative default classification, explicit opt-in for any change that marks a probe as advisory.
Risk: quota rules could starve important background processing. Mitigation: reserve minimal background quota and provide safe-list for control-plane tenants.
Risk: increased admission-path latency from quota checks. Mitigation: in-memory token buckets, local caching, fall back to eventual consistency for non-SLA-critical checks.
